title: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer and Others
bench: R.M. Lodha, C.J., Kurian Joseph, R.F. Nariman, JJ.
full_text:
An electronic record by way of secondary evidence shall not be admitted in evidence unless the mandatory requirements and certificate contemplated under Section 65B(4) of the Evidence Act are satisfied.

Oral evidence cannot substitute the mandatory certificate under Section 65B. The person who gives the certificate must state that to the best of their knowledge and belief, the information contained in the certificate is true.

Secondary evidence of electronic records is inadmissible without Section 65B compliance.

title: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
bench: R.F. Nariman, S. Ravindra Bhat, V. Ramasubramanian, JJ.
full_text:
The certificate required under Section 65B(4) is a condition precedent to the admissibility of electronic evidence as secondary evidence.

The certificate should ideally be produced when the electronic record is produced, but the court may allow it to be filed prior to the trial concluding.

In cases where an adverse party or third party refuses to produce the certificate, the court may invoke its powers under Section 165 of the Evidence Act or Order XVI CPC to compel production.

title: Vidya Drolia and Others v. Durga Trading Corporation
bench: N.V. Ramana, Sanjiv Khanna, Krishna Murari, JJ.
full_text:
A dispute is non-arbitrable when: (1) it relates to actions in rem; (2) affects third-party rights or has erga omnes effect; (3) pertains to inalienable sovereign functions; or (4) is expressly or by necessary implication non-arbitrable under a specific statute.

Landlord-tenant disputes governed by the Transfer of Property Act are arbitrable unless covered by special rent control legislation.

title: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra
bench: T.S. Thakur, Vikramajit Sen, C. Nagappan, JJ.
full_text:
Jurisdiction to file a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act lies where the drawee bank is located.

This was subsequently amended by the Negotiable Instruments Amendment Act 2015 to locate jurisdiction at the branch where payee maintains their account.

title: Babulal Vardharji Gurjar v. Veer Gurjar Aluminium Industries Pvt. Ltd.
full_text:
The period of limitation for filing an application under Section 7 of the IBC is three years governed by Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, commencing from the date when default occurred.

An acknowledgement under Section 18 can extend limitation only if pleaded with specific foundation.
